Title: 15th of June: Morning discussion with Fernando Meirelles
Chunks: 0,1
On the Saturday morning discussion, Brazilian director **Fernando Meirelles** told about his versatile career, which has included various works from video art to successful international films and from experimental TV series to opera.
Meirelles remembers his first film experiences are related to his father’s movie clips which were shot on 16mm film. However, the career as a director was not Meirelles’s original plan. He grew up in São Paulo and after discontinuing his biology studies Meirelles studied architecture. He decided to become a filmmaker after seeing **Jorge Bodanzky** and **Orlando Senna**’s _Iracema_ (1975). It was a film that combined fiction and documentary such an exceptional way and was so impressive for Meirelles that he decided to make a short film as his final project and, as a result, made his introduction to the film industry.
At the beginning of his career, Meirelles and his colleagues made experimental short films and video art. He also directed several years fun and experimental series and worked in advertising. However, the ads were not enough for Meirelles – instead, he dreamed of directing a feature film. He practiced directing a feature film with his first film _Maids_ (2001).
“I always want to get involved in projects that make me feel insecure. The topics I don’t know much about and I usually even regret, that I agreed to take on such an impossible idea. For some reason, these work the best in the end.”
Meirelles wanted to film **José Saramago**‘s novel _Blindness_, but because of the copyrights, the plan was almost canceled. One of the luckiest coincidences on Meirelles’s career was when the publisher of Saramago asked if Meirelles would be interested in directing **Paulo Lins**‘s novel _The City of God_. After a short moment of hesitation, Meirelles grasped this opportunity and chose a completely different topic.

Meirelles’s The City of God was screened at the Cannes Film Festival and was a great success. The film was followed by another success, _The Constant Gardener_ (2005), after which Meirelles announced that he would stop making movies. However, he went back on his decision, as he finally got the opportunity to direct a film adaption of Blindness (2008). The film was followed by _360_ (2011) and then Meirelles returned to TV series. Even after that the director has still broken new ground.
Trying something new has always inspired Meirelles. He has directed, for example, the opera _Les Pêcheurs de Perles_ in 2015 and the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro in 2016. Currently, the director has many projects in progress, including a climate crisis series for the BBC, a science documentary and the feature film _The Pope_ produced by Netflix.
Meirelles would bring the film Iracema with him to a deserted island. That movie which originally encouraged him to become a director.

## Texto
![Image 1: Abrir módulo](https://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/packs/media/images/general/icon-arrow-down-c34972d6de930883a1a6b59a5869ffe9.svg)
Jorge Bodanzky (São Paulo, São Paulo, 1942). Fotógrafo, diretor. Interessa-se por fotografia na juventude. Em 1965, ingressa na faculdade de arquitetura da Universidade de Brasília, onde se aproxima do curso de cinema implementado por [Paulo Emílio Salles Gomes (1916-1977)](https://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/pessoas/1865-paulo-emilio-salles-gomes), [Jean Claude Bernardet (1936)](https://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/pessoas/474-jean-claude-bernardet), [Nelson Pereira dos Santos (1928)](https://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/pessoas/23987-nelson-pereira-dos-santos), entre outros. Com o fechamento do curso pela ditadura militar, passa a atuar como repórter fotográfico. Em 1966, obtém uma bolsa para estudar fotografia na Escola Superior da Forma em Ulm, Alemanha. O departamento de cinema, para onde se transfere, é coordenado pelo diretor alemão Alexander Kluge (1932). Lá, especializa-se em fotografia de cinema. Também conhece seu futuro parceiro de documentários e longas, Wolf Gauer. Retornando ao Brasil em 1968, trabalha como repórter fotográfico na revista Realidade e faz seus primeiros trabalhos como fotógrafo de cinema em curtas documentais e longas de ficção, como _Hitler 3º Mundo_ (1968), _Gamal, O Delírio do Sexo_ (1969) e _O Profeta da Fome_(1969).

## Texto
Dirige com Hermano Penna (1945) e fotografa o curta _Caminhos de Valderez_(1971). Ainda no início de 1970, retorna à Alemanha, onde trabalha como fotógrafo de reportagens e documentários para a TV. Funda a Stopfilm (1972) em Munique com Wolf Gauer, para produzir documentários sobre o Brasil e a América Latina. Nesta época, faz as primeiras incursões à Amazônia. A partir de 1973, trabalha em São Paulo, quando fotografa o documentário _O Fabuloso Fittipaldi_(1973) de Roberto Farias (1932).
No ano seguinte, financiado pela TV alemã, retorna a Amazônia para rodar [_Iracema – Uma Transa Amazônica_(1974)](https://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/obras/123474-iracema-uma-transa-amazonica), filme em 16 mm, som direto, com codireção de Orlando Senna (1940) e uma pequena equipe de filmagem. Premiado internacionalmente após o lançamento, o filme é vetado pela censura até o início da década de 1980. Em 1975, com a mesma equipe e coprodução alemã, Bodansky e Senna partem para o sertão nordestino e realizam o longa-metragem _Gitirana_ (1976). O filme participa da quinzena dos realizadores do Festival de Cannes, mas é censurado por mais de 5 anos no Brasil. Filma o documentário de média-metragem Jari (1979), sobre o Projeto Jari na Amazônia.

## Texto
Entre os anos 1970 e 1980, continua com Wolf Gauer a dirigir documentários para a TV alemã, como Wolkswagen: Operários na Alemanha e no Brasil (1974). Com codireção de Gauer, realiza _Os Mucker_(1978), também com apoio da TV alemã. Em 1981, filma a campanha para a reeleição do senador amazonense Evandro Carreira (1927-2015), o _Terceiro Milênio_. Ainda em 1981, _Iracema – Uma Transa Amazônica_ é relançado e recebe o Candango de melhor filme no Festival de Brasília. Realiza para o Globo Repórter, _Amazônia, O Último Eldorado_(1982). Retorna ao longa documental com _Igreja dos Oprimidos_ (1986) em parceria de Helena Salem (1948-1999). Dos anos 1990 em diante, continua realizando documentários de curtas e médias metragens, tal como a fotografia do documentário _À Margem do Concreto_(2006) de Evaldo Mocarzel (1960). Produz CD-ROMs como _Amazônia – Um Fantástico Universo_(1996) e dedica-se à produção fotográfica tematizando a relação cultura e meio ambiente.

**William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.

Condon was born in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on October 22, 1955,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-ibdb-2) the son of a police [detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective "Detective"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-3) and was raised in an [Irish Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic "Irish Catholic") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-5) He attended [Regis High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(New_York_City) "Regis High School (New York City)") and [Columbia College of Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_of_Columbia_University "Columbia College of Columbia University"), graduating in 1976 with a degree in philosophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
Two films had a significant impact of Condon's early life. At the age of twelve, he found himself drawn to screenplay writing with his first viewing of [_Bonnie and Clyde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde_(film) "Bonnie and Clyde (film)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-6) In college he saw _[Sweet Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Charity\_(film) "Sweet Charity (film)")_ (1969), which led to "a lifelong love affair with movies that are reviled and rejected in their time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

Condon wrote and directed _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_ (1998), which was based on a novel by [Christopher Bram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Bram "Christopher Bram"). His screenplay won the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay"). _The New York Times_ said Condon "may have been the most stunned person at the Academy Awards when his name was announced as the winner for the best adapted screenplay. He has struggled for years in Hollywood as a screenwriter and journalist and is unaccustomed to the hoopla that is now around him."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-15) He was nominated for the same award for his screenplay for _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, based on the Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(musical) "Chicago (musical)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-16) He received a second Edgar Award for his _Chicago_ screenplay as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-17)

In 2004 he wrote and directed the film _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, chronicling the life of the controversial sex researcher [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey"). In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." He continued: "I can't think of another movie that has dealt with sex so knowledgeably and, at the same time, made the pursuit of knowledge seem so sexy. There are some explicit images and provocative scenes, but it is your intellect that is most likely to be aroused.... Mr. Condon's great achievement is to turn Kinsey's complicated and controversial career into a grand intellectual drama."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-18)
In 2005, he received the [Stephen F. Kolzak Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Awards "GLAAD Media Awards") at the [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") Media Awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-19)
Condon wrote the screenplay for and directed _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, an adaptation of the acclaimed Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls "Dreamgirls"). It was released in December 2006. Condon received [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominations for directing. The film was nominated for eight Academy Awards in six categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-20)

Condon was executive producer of the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") television broadcast that aired on February 22, 2009, working with producer [Laurence Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Mark "Laurence Mark").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-21)
Condon directed both parts of _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Dawn\_(disambiguation) "Breaking Dawn (disambiguation)")_ (2011 and 2012), adapted from the fourth and final novel in _[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(novel\_series) "Twilight (novel series)")_ by [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer"). He was twice nominated for a [Razzie for Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director") for these films, winning for _Part 2_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-22)
Condon directed _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ (2013), a thriller about [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") starring [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch"). He said he chose the project for a change of pace and liked its non-ideological approach to a very complex subject. He saw it "in the great tradition of journalistic thrillers".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-23) It received mixed responses from critics and underperformed at the box office.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-24)

In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)
In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)

In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)
In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)
Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)

_**The Fifth Estate**_ is a 2013 [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film")[thriller film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_film "Thriller film") directed by [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon") about the [news-leaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_leak "News leak") website [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks").

The film stars [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch") as its editor-in-chief and founder [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange") and [Daniel Brühl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Br%C3%BChl "Daniel Brühl") as its former spokesperson [Daniel Domscheit-Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Domscheit-Berg "Daniel Domscheit-Berg").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-bcjafirstlook-7)[Anthony Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mackie "Anthony Mackie"), [David Thewlis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Thewlis "David Thewlis"), [Alicia Vikander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Vikander "Alicia Vikander"), [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci"), and [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney") are featured in supporting roles.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-8) The film's screenplay was written by [Josh Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Singer "Josh Singer") based in-part on Domscheit-Berg's book _Inside WikiLeaks: My Time with Julian Assange at the World's Most Dangerous Website_ (2011), as well as _[WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks:\_Inside\_Julian\_Assange's\_War\_on\_Secrecy "WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy")_ (2011) by British journalists [David Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Leigh_(journalist) "David Leigh (journalist)") and [Luke Harding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Harding_(journalist) "Luke Harding (journalist)").

The [film's name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_estate "Fifth estate") is a reference to people who operate in the manner of journalists outside the normal constraints imposed on the mainstream media.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-9)

*   [Dan Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Stevens "Dan Stevens") as [Ian Katz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Katz "Ian Katz")

It was reported in March 2011 that [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")'s [DreamWorks Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamWorks_Studios "DreamWorks Studios") had acquired the rights of Domscheit-Berg's book _Inside WikiLeaks: My Time with Julian Assange and the World's Most Dangerous Website_, as well as _WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy_ by British journalists David Leigh and Luke Harding.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-17) Spielberg was quick to clarify that he is not involved in any way in the adaptation even though his DreamWorks company would produce the film.

In July 2012, reports surfaced that [Jeremy Renner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Renner "Jeremy Renner") was in talks of playing [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange"), and [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon") was in negotiations to direct. It was also announced that [Josh Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Singer "Josh Singer") penned the screenplay. Later that year, _Deadline Hollywood_ broke the news that Renner was out of the running and the studio was seeking [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch") instead.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-18)[Joel Kinnaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Kinnaman "Joel Kinnaman") was also attached at some point, but reports were proven to be premature. The confirmation of Cumberbatch as the lead and Condon as the director also brought the news that [James McAvoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_McAvoy "James McAvoy") was in talks to play [Daniel Domscheit-Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Domscheit-Berg "Daniel Domscheit-Berg").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-19) McAvoy later dropped out because of scheduling conflicts and [Daniel Brühl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Br%C3%BChl "Daniel Brühl") was eventually cast.
In December 2012, the film's title was reported as _The Man Who Sold the World_[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-20) but with the official press release, it was confirmed that the film's title was actually _The Fifth Estate_.

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on January 23, 2013, with [Michael Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sugar "Michael Sugar") and [Steve Golin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Golin "Steve Golin") of [Anonymous Content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymous_Content "Anonymous Content") serving as producers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-DisneyPress-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-21) During filming, Cumberbatch had to wear three different wigs, false teeth and blue [contact lenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact_lenses "Contact lenses"), in order to reflect Julian Assange's physical characteristics.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-22)
The film was partially shot in Belgium, as can be seen in the movie poster, which contains the [Liège-Guillemins railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge-Guillemins_railway_station "Liège-Guillemins railway station").
The film's title sequence, which depicts the history of news communication, took over a year to create.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-23)
The film's score was composed by [Carter Burwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Burwell "Carter Burwell") and its soundtrack was released by [Lakeshore Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakeshore_Records "Lakeshore Records") on October 8, 2013.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-24)

texts.2: **William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.

Condon was born in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on October 22, 1955,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-ibdb-2) the son of a police [detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective "Detective"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-3) and was raised in an [Irish Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic "Irish Catholic") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-5) He attended [Regis High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(New_York_City) "Regis High School (New York City)") and [Columbia College of Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_of_Columbia_University "Columbia College of Columbia University"), graduating in 1976 with a degree in philosophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
Two films had a significant impact of Condon's early life. At the age of twelve, he found himself drawn to screenplay writing with his first viewing of [_Bonnie and Clyde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde_(film) "Bonnie and Clyde (film)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-6) In college he saw _[Sweet Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Charity\_(film) "Sweet Charity (film)")_ (1969), which led to "a lifelong love affair with movies that are reviled and rejected in their time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
texts.6: Condon wrote and directed _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_ (1998), which was based on a novel by [Christopher Bram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Bram "Christopher Bram"). His screenplay won the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay"). _The New York Times_ said Condon "may have been the most stunned person at the Academy Awards when his name was announced as the winner for the best adapted screenplay. He has struggled for years in Hollywood as a screenwriter and journalist and is unaccustomed to the hoopla that is now around him."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-15) He was nominated for the same award for his screenplay for _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, based on the Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(musical) "Chicago (musical)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-16) He received a second Edgar Award for his _Chicago_ screenplay as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-17)
texts.7:
In 2004 he wrote and directed the film _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, chronicling the life of the controversial sex researcher [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey"). In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." He continued: "I can't think of another movie that has dealt with sex so knowledgeably and, at the same time, made the pursuit of knowledge seem so sexy. There are some explicit images and provocative scenes, but it is your intellect that is most likely to be aroused.... Mr. Condon's great achievement is to turn Kinsey's complicated and controversial career into a grand intellectual drama."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-18)
In 2005, he received the [Stephen F. Kolzak Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Awards "GLAAD Media Awards") at the [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") Media Awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-19)
Condon wrote the screenplay for and directed _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, an adaptation of the acclaimed Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls "Dreamgirls"). It was released in December 2006. Condon received [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominations for directing. The film was nominated for eight Academy Awards in six categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-20)
texts.8:
Condon was executive producer of the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") television broadcast that aired on February 22, 2009, working with producer [Laurence Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Mark "Laurence Mark").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-21)
Condon directed both parts of _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Dawn\_(disambiguation) "Breaking Dawn (disambiguation)")_ (2011 and 2012), adapted from the fourth and final novel in _[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(novel\_series) "Twilight (novel series)")_ by [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer"). He was twice nominated for a [Razzie for Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director") for these films, winning for _Part 2_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-22)
Condon directed _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ (2013), a thriller about [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") starring [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch"). He said he chose the project for a change of pace and liked its non-ideological approach to a very complex subject. He saw it "in the great tradition of journalistic thrillers".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-23) It received mixed responses from critics and underperformed at the box office.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-24)
texts.9:
In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)
In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)
texts.12:
In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)
In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)
Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)

_**The Fifth Estate**_ is a 2013 [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film")[thriller film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_film "Thriller film") directed by [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon") about the [news-leaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_leak "News leak") website [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks").
texts.3: The film stars [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch") as its editor-in-chief and founder [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange") and [Daniel Brühl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Br%C3%BChl "Daniel Brühl") as its former spokesperson [Daniel Domscheit-Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Domscheit-Berg "Daniel Domscheit-Berg").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-bcjafirstlook-7)[Anthony Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mackie "Anthony Mackie"), [David Thewlis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Thewlis "David Thewlis"), [Alicia Vikander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Vikander "Alicia Vikander"), [Stanley Tucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Tucci "Stanley Tucci"), and [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney") are featured in supporting roles.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-8) The film's screenplay was written by [Josh Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Singer "Josh Singer") based in-part on Domscheit-Berg's book _Inside WikiLeaks: My Time with Julian Assange at the World's Most Dangerous Website_ (2011), as well as _[WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks:\_Inside\_Julian\_Assange's\_War\_on\_Secrecy "WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy")_ (2011) by British journalists [David Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Leigh_(journalist) "David Leigh (journalist)") and [Luke Harding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Harding_(journalist) "Luke Harding (journalist)").
texts.4: The [film's name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_estate "Fifth estate") is a reference to people who operate in the manner of journalists outside the normal constraints imposed on the mainstream media.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-9)

It was reported in March 2011 that [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")'s [DreamWorks Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamWorks_Studios "DreamWorks Studios") had acquired the rights of Domscheit-Berg's book _Inside WikiLeaks: My Time with Julian Assange and the World's Most Dangerous Website_, as well as _WikiLeaks: Inside Julian Assange's War on Secrecy_ by British journalists David Leigh and Luke Harding.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-17) Spielberg was quick to clarify that he is not involved in any way in the adaptation even though his DreamWorks company would produce the film.
texts.12:
In July 2012, reports surfaced that [Jeremy Renner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Renner "Jeremy Renner") was in talks of playing [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange"), and [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon") was in negotiations to direct. It was also announced that [Josh Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Singer "Josh Singer") penned the screenplay. Later that year, _Deadline Hollywood_ broke the news that Renner was out of the running and the studio was seeking [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch") instead.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-18)[Joel Kinnaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Kinnaman "Joel Kinnaman") was also attached at some point, but reports were proven to be premature. The confirmation of Cumberbatch as the lead and Condon as the director also brought the news that [James McAvoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_McAvoy "James McAvoy") was in talks to play [Daniel Domscheit-Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Domscheit-Berg "Daniel Domscheit-Berg").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-19) McAvoy later dropped out because of scheduling conflicts and [Daniel Brühl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Br%C3%BChl "Daniel Brühl") was eventually cast.
In December 2012, the film's title was reported as _The Man Who Sold the World_[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-20) but with the official press release, it was confirmed that the film's title was actually _The Fifth Estate_.
texts.13:
[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on January 23, 2013, with [Michael Sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sugar "Michael Sugar") and [Steve Golin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Golin "Steve Golin") of [Anonymous Content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymous_Content "Anonymous Content") serving as producers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-DisneyPress-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-21) During filming, Cumberbatch had to wear three different wigs, false teeth and blue [contact lenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact_lenses "Contact lenses"), in order to reflect Julian Assange's physical characteristics.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-22)
The film was partially shot in Belgium, as can be seen in the movie poster, which contains the [Liège-Guillemins railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge-Guillemins_railway_station "Liège-Guillemins railway station").
The film's title sequence, which depicts the history of news communication, took over a year to create.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-23)
The film's score was composed by [Carter Burwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Burwell "Carter Burwell") and its soundtrack was released by [Lakeshore Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakeshore_Records "Lakeshore Records") on October 8, 2013.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fifth_Estate_(film)#cite_note-24)

_**The Constant Gardener**_ is a 2005 [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)") film[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-3) directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles"). The screenplay by [Jeffrey Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Caine "Jeffrey Caine") is based on [John le Carré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_le_Carr%C3%A9 "John le Carré")'s [2001 novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener "The Constant Gardener"). The story follows Justin Quayle ([Ralph Fiennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Fiennes "Ralph Fiennes")), a British diplomat in Kenya, as he tries to solve the murder of his wife Tessa ([Rachel Weisz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz "Rachel Weisz")), an [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist, alternating with [flashbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)") telling the story of their relationship.
The film's title derives from Justin's gentle but diligent attention to his plants throughout the film. The film was a critical and box office success and earned four [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations, winning [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for Weisz.

British diplomat and avid horticulturalist Justin Quayle is confronted by [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist Tessa during a lecture in London. They strike up a romance, and marry after she accompanies him to his posting in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). She befriends Belgian doctor Arnold Bluhm, leading to rumours of an affair. Tessa has no qualms confronting corruption, to the chagrin of Justin's superiors, and she loses a child late in pregnancy.
Tessa and Arnold connect recent local deaths to [drug trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial "Clinical trial") being conducted by the Kenyan-based company Three Bees using the drug Dypraxa. They write a damaging report on the drug and Tessa gives it to Justin's colleague Sandy Woodrow, the British [High Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Commissioner "High Commissioner"), who sends it to Sir Bernard Pellegrin, head of the Africa Desk at the [Foreign Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign,_Commonwealth_and_Development_Office "Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office"). Pellegrin responds with an incriminating letter to Sandy, which Tessa persuades him to show her, and she steals it before departing for [Lokichogio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokichogio "Lokichogio") with Arnold.
Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near [Lake Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana "Lake Turkana"), and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at [Lodwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodwar "Lodwar") before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.

After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as [homosexuality is illegal in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Kenya "LGBT rights in Kenya"). Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, [Swiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland")-[Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")[pharmaceutical conglomerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects. Curtiss points Justin to Dr Lorbeer, Dypraxa's inventor, who has fled to [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"). Tim Donohue, a friend in British intelligence, confirms that Pellegrin had Tessa and Arnold killed. Unable to convince Justin to return home, he gives him a gun.

Justin travels to confront Lorbeer, who is treating remote villagers to atone for the lives claimed by his drug. The village is attacked by raiders, but Justin and Lorbeer escape in a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") aid plane, and Lorbeer reveals that he has Pellegrin's letter. Tessa convinced him to record the truth about Dypraxa, but he changed his mind, instead informing KDH that Tessa and Arnold were en route to expose the company to the UN.
Justin convinces the pilot to mail Pellegrin's letter to Ham, and to drop him off at Lake Turkana. Removing the bullets from his gun, his final thoughts are of Tessa before he is killed by KDH's henchmen. In London at Tessa and Justin's memorial service, Pellegrin lies that Justin committed suicide in the same place his wife died.
Ham announces the reading of an [epistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistle "Epistle"), but instead reads Pellegrin's letter, exposing the deaths caused by Dypraxa and the subsequent coverup. Pellegrin storms out as Ham implicates the British government, KDH, and public complacency regarding the human cost of medicine they take for granted.

## Inspiration and themes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Constant_Gardener_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Inspiration and themes")]
The plot of the film is loosely based on a [real-life case in Kano, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullahi_v._Pfizer,_Inc. "Abdullahi v. Pfizer, Inc.") involving antibacterial testing by Pfizer on small children.
The film was shot partly in [16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16mm "16mm")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-4) on location in [Loiyangalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loiyangalani "Loiyangalani") and the slums of [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), a section of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Circumstances in the area so affected the cast and crew that producer [Simon Channing Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Channing_Williams "Simon Channing Williams") led the creation of the Constant Gardener Trust in order to address issues of sanitation and education in the area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-7)
Principal photography of the film occurred from May 10, 2004 to August 7, 2004.
[Kate Winslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Winslet "Kate Winslet") and [Eva Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Green "Eva Green") were considered for the female lead before Weisz was cast.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-8)

_**The Constant Gardener**_ is a 2005 [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)") film[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-3) directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles"). The screenplay by [Jeffrey Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Caine "Jeffrey Caine") is based on [John le Carré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_le_Carr%C3%A9 "John le Carré")'s [2001 novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener "The Constant Gardener"). The story follows Justin Quayle ([Ralph Fiennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Fiennes "Ralph Fiennes")), a British diplomat in Kenya, as he tries to solve the murder of his wife Tessa ([Rachel Weisz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz "Rachel Weisz")), an [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist, alternating with [flashbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)") telling the story of their relationship.
The film's title derives from Justin's gentle but diligent attention to his plants throughout the film. The film was a critical and box office success and earned four [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations, winning [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for Weisz.
texts.3:
British diplomat and avid horticulturalist Justin Quayle is confronted by [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist Tessa during a lecture in London. They strike up a romance, and marry after she accompanies him to his posting in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). She befriends Belgian doctor Arnold Bluhm, leading to rumours of an affair. Tessa has no qualms confronting corruption, to the chagrin of Justin's superiors, and she loses a child late in pregnancy.
Tessa and Arnold connect recent local deaths to [drug trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial "Clinical trial") being conducted by the Kenyan-based company Three Bees using the drug Dypraxa. They write a damaging report on the drug and Tessa gives it to Justin's colleague Sandy Woodrow, the British [High Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Commissioner "High Commissioner"), who sends it to Sir Bernard Pellegrin, head of the Africa Desk at the [Foreign Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign,_Commonwealth_and_Development_Office "Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office"). Pellegrin responds with an incriminating letter to Sandy, which Tessa persuades him to show her, and she steals it before departing for [Lokichogio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokichogio "Lokichogio") with Arnold.
Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near [Lake Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana "Lake Turkana"), and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at [Lodwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodwar "Lodwar") before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.
texts.4:
After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as [homosexuality is illegal in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Kenya "LGBT rights in Kenya"). Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, [Swiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland")-[Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")[pharmaceutical conglomerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects. Curtiss points Justin to Dr Lorbeer, Dypraxa's inventor, who has fled to [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"). Tim Donohue, a friend in British intelligence, confirms that Pellegrin had Tessa and Arnold killed. Unable to convince Justin to return home, he gives him a gun.
texts.5:
Justin travels to confront Lorbeer, who is treating remote villagers to atone for the lives claimed by his drug. The village is attacked by raiders, but Justin and Lorbeer escape in a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") aid plane, and Lorbeer reveals that he has Pellegrin's letter. Tessa convinced him to record the truth about Dypraxa, but he changed his mind, instead informing KDH that Tessa and Arnold were en route to expose the company to the UN.
Justin convinces the pilot to mail Pellegrin's letter to Ham, and to drop him off at Lake Turkana. Removing the bullets from his gun, his final thoughts are of Tessa before he is killed by KDH's henchmen. In London at Tessa and Justin's memorial service, Pellegrin lies that Justin committed suicide in the same place his wife died.
Ham announces the reading of an [epistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistle "Epistle"), but instead reads Pellegrin's letter, exposing the deaths caused by Dypraxa and the subsequent coverup. Pellegrin storms out as Ham implicates the British government, KDH, and public complacency regarding the human cost of medicine they take for granted.

## Inspiration and themes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Constant_Gardener_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Inspiration and themes")]
The plot of the film is loosely based on a [real-life case in Kano, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullahi_v._Pfizer,_Inc. "Abdullahi v. Pfizer, Inc.") involving antibacterial testing by Pfizer on small children.
The film was shot partly in [16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16mm "16mm")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-4) on location in [Loiyangalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loiyangalani "Loiyangalani") and the slums of [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), a section of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Circumstances in the area so affected the cast and crew that producer [Simon Channing Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Channing_Williams "Simon Channing Williams") led the creation of the Constant Gardener Trust in order to address issues of sanitation and education in the area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-7)
Principal photography of the film occurred from May 10, 2004 to August 7, 2004.
[Kate Winslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Winslet "Kate Winslet") and [Eva Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Green "Eva Green") were considered for the female lead before Weisz was cast.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-8)

**Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (yavutse 25 Gicurasi 1978), uzwi cyane nka **Peter King**, ni umukinnyi wa firime muri [Kenya](https://rw.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") . Nzioki yavutse ku ya 25 Gicurasi 1978 i Nairobi, muri [Kenya](https://rw.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Se wa Michael David Mwania, yakoraga mu gisirikare cya Kenya naho nyina akora mu bitaro bya gisirikare. Afite imyaka itandatu, yinjiye mu rusengero mu kigo cya Lang'ata. Yatangiye gukina filime mu 2000 muri Theatre yigihugu ya Kenya imyaka itatu iyobowe na Joab Kanuka. Mu ikinamico, yakinnye 'Iago' muri Phoenix Players yerekana ibyago bya Shakespeare _Othello_ . Muri 2005, yakinnye bwa mbere muri firime afite uruhare ruto muri _[The Constant Gardener](https://rw.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ iyobowe na Fernando Meirelles . Yagaragaye cyane nka 'Mkwajo' muri muzika _Mo Faya_ yatsindiye ibihembo iyobowe na Eric Wainaina; umugambi _mubisha muri FaceBook_ numunyapolitiki ruswa 'Mzito' muri _Ni Sisi_ . Nyuma yinshingano nyinshi zubugome, yahawe umwanya wo kuba papa muri _serivise ya_ MTV Shuga 2, hanyuma aba umutoza wumupira wamaguru muri _The Inside Story_ yerekanwe kuri Discovery Channel; n'umuvugabutumwa mu _Cyuma Cyuma Cyuma_ . The **Goat** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"):[羊](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%BE%8A "wikt:羊"); [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"):_yáng_, sometimes also translated **Sheep** or **Ram**) is the eighth of the 12-year cycle of animals which appear in the [Chinese zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_zodiac "Chinese zodiac") related to the [Chinese calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_calendar "Chinese calendar"). This zodiacal sign is often[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-huang-1) referred to as the "Ram" or "Sheep" sign,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-2) since the [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language") word _yáng_ is more accurately translated as [Caprinae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caprinae "Caprinae"), a [taxonomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomic_rank "Taxonomic rank")[subfamily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subfamily "Subfamily") that includes both goats and sheep,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-3) but contrasts with other animal [subfamily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subfamily "Subfamily") types such as [Bovinae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bovinae "Bovinae"), [Antilopinae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antilopinae "Antilopinae"), and other taxonomic considerations which may be encountered in the case of the larger family of [Bovidae in Chinese mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bovidae_in_Chinese_mythology "Bovidae in Chinese mythology"), which also includes the [Ox (zodiac)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ox_(zodiac) "Ox (zodiac)").

The **Year of the Goat** is associated with the 8th [Earthly Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthly_Branches "Earthly Branches")[symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbol "Symbol"), **[未](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9C%AA "wikt:未")** (_wèi_).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-4)

The [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language") word _yáng_ refers to both goats and sheep,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-5) whereas the terms _shānyáng_ (山羊) and _miányáng_ (绵羊; 綿羊) refer exclusively to goats and sheep, respectively.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-celebrating-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-7) In [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language"), the sign (originally based on a horned animal) may be called either. The interpretation of goat or sheep depends on [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-huang-1) In [Vietnamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_language "Vietnamese language"), the sign is _mùi_, which is unambiguously goat.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-cjvlang-8) In [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"), on the other hand, the sign is _hitsuji,_ sheep;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-cjvlang-8) while in [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-pearson-9)[Mongolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolia "Mongolia"), and [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), the sign is ram or sheep.

Due to the [lunisolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunisolar_calendar "Lunisolar calendar")[nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature "Nature") of the [traditional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture")[Chinese calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_calendar "Chinese calendar") system,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-12) the [zodiacal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrological_sign "Astrological sign") year does not align with the [Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar "Gregorian calendar"): new years are determined by a system which results in each new year beginning on a [new moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_moon "New moon") sometime between late January to mid-to-late February.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-pinyin-13) Goat aspects can also enter by other [chronomantic](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/chronomantic "wikt:chronomantic") factors or measures, such as hourly.
In [Chinese astrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_astrology "Chinese astrology"), Goats are described as peace-loving, kind, and popular.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-14) With the addition of the [Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood_(Wu_Xing) "Wood (Wu Xing)")[element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuxing_(Chinese_philosophy) "Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)"), the Goat characteristic is thought to love peace and to be helpful and trusting, but yet also to be clinging and resistant to change.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-15)

The interpretation of goat or sheep depends on [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-huang-1) In [Vietnamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_language "Vietnamese language"), the sign is _mùi_, which is unambiguously goat.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-cjvlang-8) In [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"), on the other hand, the sign is _hitsuji,_ sheep;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-cjvlang-8) while in [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-pearson-9)[Mongolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolia "Mongolia"), and [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), the sign is ram or sheep.

Due to the [lunisolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunisolar_calendar "Lunisolar calendar")[nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature "Nature") of the [traditional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_culture "Chinese culture")[Chinese calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_calendar "Chinese calendar") system,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-12) the [zodiacal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrological_sign "Astrological sign") year does not align with the [Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar "Gregorian calendar"): new years are determined by a system which results in each new year beginning on a [new moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_moon "New moon") sometime between late January to mid-to-late February.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_(zodiac)#cite_note-pinyin-13) Goat aspects can also enter by other [chronomantic](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/chronomantic "wikt:chronomantic") factors or measures, such as hourly.
